subject: Make lincombs dataframe to calculate probability that a spatial coefficient is below mean

messages.author: 68c425efdf6bd7f6
messages.subject: Make lincombs dataframe to calculate probability that a spatial coefficient is below mean
parts:
Dear INLA enthusiasts,

I have a spatial regression model, where two explanatory variables have a spatial effect as provided by the formula below. For those two variables (X3, X4) I would like to calculate the probability that the spatial coefficient is below the mean.  I am stuck on how to make an appropriate lincomb dataframe for the two variables. I have tried to do:


# Reg is spatial polygons dataframe where each line is an administrative unit and Y is my dependent variable and X1, X2, X3, X4 are my explanatory variables. id1 and id2 are the ids of my polygons (e.g. postal codes).

N = length(Reg$Y)
J = length(Reg$id1)

dat.inla.extra <- list(N = N,J = J)

##Linear combinations dataframe - I have only found an approach in a paper, where the author made a lincomb dataframe for one variable (I need this for two variables (X3, X4)

lcs <- inla.make.lincombs(X3= rep(1, dat.inla.extra$J),
                          id1 = diag(dat.inla.extra$J))


form1 = Y~  1 +  X1 + X2 +
  f(id1, X3, model =  "besag", graph= "graph") +
  f(id2, X4, model =  "besag", graph= "graph")
 
result = inla(form1,family="poisson", data=Reg@data, lincomb = lcs, E=E, control.inla= list(strategy = "gaussian", int.strategy = "eb"), control.compute = list(dic=T), verbose = TRUE)

However, this does not seem to work and INLA crashes when I run the model. I have three questions:

1. How should I define the lincomb dataframe?

2. How can I make the lincomb dataframe for two explanatory variables at once?

3. How can I extract the marginals and compute for both variables that the coefficients are below the mean?

Many thanks in advance!

Boris
